name: Ashy Minivet
rangeDescription: Northeastern asia; winters to philippines and indonesia
description: Slender, long-tailed gray songbird, usually seen in small to medium-sized flocks. Male has a distinct black-and-white head pattern, of which the female has a paler gray version.

name: Demoiselle Crane
rangeDescription: Palearctic; winters in northeastern africa and southern asia
description: Small gray crane of open expansive habitats. Adult is an elegantly smooth shade of gray with a black neck, fiery eyes, and pure white plumes extending out from behind the eyes.

name: Guianan Trogon
rangeDescription: Venezuela, trinidad, the guianas, and adjacent northern brazil
description: Medium-sized, long-tailed, sluggish bird that occurs in a variety of humid forest types. Males are iridescent blue with a yellow belly; females are mostly grayish where males are blue.

name: Zone-tailed Hawk
rangeDescription: Arid southwestern usa to northern bolivia, paraguay, and brazil
description: Dark raptor that soars with a

name: Campbell Islands Shag
rangeDescription: Campbell islands
description: A medium-sized, black-and-white marine shag with a metallic green-and-blue glimmer on the black head, neck, and throat. Note the white wing patches.

name: Brown-rumped Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Small, mouse-like bird found only at higher elevations in Colombia’s Santa Marta Mountains. Adult is gray with a bit of brown on the rump and lower underparts.

name: Sula Golden-Bulbul
rangeDescription: Sula islands (taliabu, mangole, and sanana)
description: A noticeably long-billed thrush-sized bird with an olive head and upperside and uniform yellow underparts. Pairs or small groups inhabit forests, edges, and plantations in the lowlands and foothills.

name: Trilling Shrike-Babbler
rangeDescription: Highlands of western java
description: Adorable stout little yellowish bird of Java’s foothill and montane forests. Male is unique, with bright yellow underparts, flashing black-and-white wingbars, dark lores, and a deep rust-red throat.

name: Geelvink Fruit-Dove
rangeDescription: Numfor, biak, and yapen (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: Localized endemic of islands in West Papua’s Geelvink Bay, including Biak and Numfor. Males have a large, bright “fried egg” yellow-and-white patch on the chest and a hot pink patch on the belly.

name: Puna Tinamou
rangeDescription: Andes of peru to northern bolivia, chile and northwestern argentina
description: Large, cryptically patterned chickenlike bird of puna grassland and bogs in the high Andes. Usually seen in trios or family groups (males take care of the young); fairly common where not hunted, but mostly wary of people.

name: Sulphur-bellied Whistler
rangeDescription: Montane forest of sulawesi
description: A fairly nondescript thick-billed, sparrow-sized songbird. Upperparts are uniform rich brown and underparts whitish, but particularly note the yellow wash to the lower belly and the base of the undertail.

name: Maleo
rangeDescription: Sulawesi including buton (off southeast), and formerly lembeh (just east of northern sulawesi)
description: A massive black-and-white megapode with a rose-pink breast and a diagnostic prominent knob on the nape. Found in lowland and hill forest, in areas near beaches or areas with volcanic sands in which they lay their eggs.

name: Violet Crow
rangeDescription: Southern moluccas (seram, buru, and ambon)
description: An entirely blackish short-tailed crow. Has a subtle purplish sheen that is visible in only certain lighting conditions.

name: Scaly Weaver
rangeDescription: Southwestern angola, namibia, far southern zambia, botswana, zimbabwe, and northern and central south africa
description: A very small, sandy-colored finch-like weaver with a scaly crown, a pale pink bill, and a black moustache on a white throat that gives it a fierce-looking expression. Small groups are resident and nomadic in grassy arid savanna, where there are trees and scrub nearby in which to build their untidy oval grass nests.

name: Wetar Scops-Owl
rangeDescription: Wetar (lesser sundas)
description: A fairly common species endemic to the island of Wetar, where the only scops-owl present. Inhabits both primary and degraded forest from lowlands to the hills.

name: Copper Seedeater
rangeDescription: Eastern and central south america, from suriname and french guiana southward to southern brazil
description: Very small finchlike bird with a short bill. Males are unmistakable—mostly cinnamon with a black cap, wings, and tail.

name: Gray Junglefowl
rangeDescription: Peninsular india
description: Common relative of the domestic chicken. Endemic to peninsular India where it occurs in deciduous and evergreen forest.

name: Tanimbar Friarbird
rangeDescription: Tanimbar islands (larat and yamdena) and kai islands (kai kecil and kai besar)
description: A very large, entirely gray-brown honeyeater with a long, heavy bill that is slightly downcurved, with a sharp, pointed tip and a clear nostril. Note the patch of naked skin below the eye.

name: Lesser Hornero
rangeDescription: Amazonian brazil, southern colombia, eastern ecuador, and northeastern peru
description: The smallest hornero. Plumage rusty overall with a white eyebrow, a gray crown, and a white throat.

name: Brown-rumped Seedeater
rangeDescription: Juniper woodland of northern ethiopia, eritrea, and northwestern somalia
description: A plain seedeater of the Abyssinian highlands. Note the gray-brown back, the paler underparts, the white eyebrow, and the small white throat.
